summary: RECOMMENDATION ONLY, not an approval. Applying the fixed stopping rule: all 8 prior findings are properly resolved in the contract text (finding 3 with a non-blocking residual), none re-raised. Two new CONFIRMED drafting defects were found, both introduced or exposed by the 0.1.2 revision: the RISK element of the six-part output structure is claimed in Responsible For but absent from the Output Schema (mismatch with the Phase 6 mitigation), and the treatment of a sampling_rule_ref while DC-7 is deferred contradicts itself across the staging paragraph, the coverage input row and step 3. Both are one-clause fixes. One PLAUSIBLE non-blocking point is routed to Known Risks. All mandatory template sections are present and sound; authority limits are not widened; scope (GD-07) and hold semantics are not raised.

findings.clause_cited: ## Responsible For bullet 7 (line 69) versus ## Output Schema (findings and reviewed_claims blocks) and ## Change Log 0.1.2; Phase 6 required mitigation in docs/ARCHITECTURE-RISKS.md section 10 ('Adopt (or explicitly extend) the CLAIM/STATUS/EVIDENCE/ASSUMPTIONS/RISK/ACTION-REQUIRED output schema')
findings.issue: [BLOCKING] Introduced by the 0.1.2 revision. Responsible For still says findings are returned in the CLAIM / STATUS / EVIDENCE / ASSUMPTIONS / RISK / ACTION REQUIRED structure, but the revision removed reviewed_claims.risk and findings.description, and no field in the Output Schema carries RISK. No clause states that the structure is being extended or that RISK is replaced by finding_type and blocking. That is both an internal contradiction and a mismatch with the Phase 6 required mitigation, which allows extension only if explicit. The fix is small: either add a closed-vocabulary RISK field (for example an enum derived from finding_type) or state in the Output Schema that RISK is replaced by finding_type and blocking and the six-part structure is extended accordingly, and correct Responsible For to match. Drafting defect, so it blocks under the stopping rule.

findings.clause_cited: ## Build Preconditions, Staging paragraph, DC-7 sentence ('any sampling_rule_ref is a stop condition') versus ## Required Inputs, Coverage entry row ('a sampling_rule_ref with no recorded human approval is rank 3 and escalates') and ## Process step 3 ('The stop conditions are those listed in the Required Inputs manifest row')
findings.issue: [BLOCKING] Internal contradiction on the same input. While DC-7 is deferred, a present sampling_rule_ref is a stop condition (step 9 rank 1: no content review, INCOMPLETE) per the staging paragraph, but an unapproved sampling_rule_ref is rank 3 per the coverage row, and the manifest row that step 3 names as the complete list of stop conditions does not include it. The two readings give different gate values on the same input when the pack also has a blocking finding (rank 3 leaves HOLD_RECOMMENDED available, rank 1 does not), and step 11(a) makes the recorder reject whichever one the agent chose. This is the same class as the precedence defect fixed in 0.1.2, in a narrower place. State one treatment (for example add 'sampling_rule_ref present while DC-7 is deferred' to the manifest row's stop conditions, or change the staging sentence to rank 3) and make step 3, the coverage row and the staging paragraph agree. Drafting defect, so it blocks under the stopping rule.

findings.clause_cited: ## Output Schema opening paragraph ('Every string the agent authors is an identifier, an enum value, a verbatim quotation ... or a closed form') versus ## Handoff Contract Returns (claims, evidence) and schemas/material-claim.schema.json (statement) and schemas/evidence.schema.json (title, source_type, timestamp)
findings.issue: [NON-BLOCKING] The no-free-text rule is stated as universal, but the handoff schemas require agent-set strings (claim statement, evidence title, source_type, timestamp) for which the contract gives no closed form or recorder-rendered value, so DC-8 check (e) as written could reject a schema-valid handoff, or the fields become the unconstrained text channel the rule is meant to remove. It is not an internal contradiction or a mismatch the contract cannot satisfy (a statement can be the recorder-format string or a closed form), so it does not meet the blocking test. Destination: Known Risks (row 'Substitute content travelling in text fields'), with a note to the Evaluation Designer and Builder that these fields are rendered by the recorder.

final_verdict_rationale: Under the stopping rule only a CONFIRMED drafting defect blocks. Findings 1 (RISK element missing from the Output Schema against Responsible For and the Phase 6 mitigation) and 2 (sampling_rule_ref stop versus rank 3 contradiction) are [BLOCKING]; finding 3 is [NON-BLOCKING] (route to Known Risks). A narrow Architect revision for findings 1 and 2 only is required, then one more review; remaining items then go to the Project Owner. Nothing here is approved; only the Project Owner can approve, and any override must be logged under GD-01.

handoff.request: Third review pass, under the fixed stopping rule, of the Assurance Reviewer contract version 0.1.2: verify the 8 prior findings are resolved in the contract text and raise only findings that are both CONFIRMED and drafting defects as blocking.
findings: 1 | BLOCKING | CONFIRMED | Responsible For bullet 7 vs Output Schema: RISK element of the six-part structure claimed but absent; Phase 6 mitigation requires adopt or explicitly extend
2 | BLOCKING | CONFIRMED | Build Preconditions staging (DC-7) vs Required Inputs coverage row vs Process step 3: sampling_rule_ref is a rank 1 stop in one place, rank 3 in another
3 | NON-BLOCKING | PLAUSIBLE | Schema-required agent-set strings (claim statement, evidence title, source_type, timestamp) have no closed form; route to Known Risks

claims.statement: Prior finding 1 (handoff.status mapping) is resolved in the contract text: the table is a total function of the step 9 outcome, escalated is used for real-data provenance and self-review, and blocked is never emitted.

Prior finding 2 (producer-controlled packet) is resolved: DC-1 has a mechanical, non-judgemental duty, the yes/no contradiction declaration is gone, and the withheld-evidence residual is stated and confidence-capped.

Prior finding 3 (free-text drift) is resolved in substance: free-text fields were removed and replaced by identifiers, enums, closed forms and verified quotations with a recorder check. One residual (schema-required strings) is raised as non-blocking finding 3.
Prior finding 4 (gate precedence contradiction) is resolved: step 9 is the only statement of the rule and other clauses defer to it.

Prior finding 5 (under-reporting) is resolved as a stated limit: Known Risks names the residual, the recorder is not presented as the answer, and added checks and a human sample are specified. The residual is a plainly stated limit and is closed.
Prior finding 6 (agent-authored evidence circular) is resolved: verbatim-quotation rule, DC-8 check (d) and a Partially supported cap until it exists.
Prior finding 7 (version and change log) is resolved: version 0.1.2 with three change-log rows.

Prior finding 8 (proportionality of eight preconditions) is closed as an owner matter: scope is decided by GD-07, staging is carried as an assumption pending the owner, and the contract decides nothing it should not.
Responsible For bullet 7 claims a six-part CLAIM/STATUS/EVIDENCE/ASSUMPTIONS/RISK/ACTION REQUIRED structure that the Output Schema no longer carries, against the Phase 6 required mitigation.
The staging paragraph and the coverage input row treat a present sampling_rule_ref differently (rank 1 stop versus rank 3), and step 3 lists neither.
Whether to stage DC-5 and DC-7, and whether a hold is advisory or a hard gate, are Project Owner decisions not taken by this review.
Whether the assumption-marked owner decisions (staging, sampling of clean records) are acceptable cannot be determined from the contract text.
